question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP

decoded.protected-resource-metadata: 200; authorization_servers: https://auth.mcp.opal.optimizely.com; scopes_supported: mcp:tools; bearer_methods_supported: header
decoded.authorization-server-metadata: 200 at https://auth.mcp.opal.optimizely.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server; registration_endpoint present; token auth client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, none; PKCE S256; grants authorization_code, refresh_token; scopes_supported openid, profile, email, offline_access, mcp:tools
decoded.rest: GET https://api.optimizely.com/v2/projects with no Authorization header answers 401 {"code": "invalid_credentials", "message": "Missing authorization header"}

finding: With no credentials, an MCP initialize POST to exp.mcp.opal.optimizely.com/mcp answers 401 with a JSON body (Authentication required.) and a Bearer challenge naming a realm and the protected-resource metadata, which is at the host's root rather than under the /mcp path. The metadata names auth.mcp.opal.optimizely.com as the authorization server and one resource scope, mcp:tools; that server advertises dynamic registration, confidential and public clients, PKCE S256 and five scopes in all. The Web Experimentation REST API answers a keyless GET with 401 invalid_credentials and no challenge. Same shape on 2026-09-09, 2026-09-16 and today. Nothing here measures what either surface does with a credential.

reproducibility.command: curl -sS -i -X POST https://exp.mcp.opal.optimizely.com/mcp -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"public-agents-researcher","version":"1.0"}}}'
